1. (Currently amended) A system for treating obesity, the system comprising: a gastric space filler comprising a first balloon connected to a second balloon by a conduit, wherein the gastric space filler is configured to occupy a substantial volume of a gastric cavity in the human patient in an inflated state; and an instrument throughput channel extending through the conduit, wherein the instrument throughput channel is configured to receive instruments, wherein the first balloon and the second balloon are configured to be inflated with a fluid to create a mechanical barrier that reduces food intake and promotes satiety in the patient.

2. (Currently amended) The system of claim 31 wherein the conduit comprises a first lumen in fluid communication with the first balloon, a second lumen in fluid communication with the second balloon, and a third lumen defining the instrument throughput channel, wherein the first and second lumens are configured to independently control inflation and deflation of the first and second balloons.

3. (Currently amended) The system of claim 31 wherein the conduit has an axial length, and wherein the instrument throughput channel extends along the axial length, and wherein the instrument throughput channel is sized to accommodate passage of a guide wire or endoscopic instrument for therapeutic intervention within the gastric cavity.

4. (Currently amended) The system of claim 31 wherein the gastric space filler further comprises a coupling mechanism configured to facilitate engagement with a retrieval device for removal of the gastric space filler from the gastric cavity via the esophagus, wherein the coupling mechanism comprises at least one of: a plug, a purse-string suture, a hook, or a loop structure that mechanically engages with a corresponding retrieval instrument to enable controlled extraction of the gastric space filler.

5. (Previously presented) The system of claim 31 wherein in the first and second balloons are made from at least one of the following: silicone, latex, polyethylene, polyurethane, and nylon.

6. (Currently amended) The system of claim 31 wherein the conduit comprises an inter-balloon section spacing the first balloon apart from the second balloon, and wherein the inter-balloon section has a length of about __15-35 mm__.

7. (Cancelled)

8. (Cancelled)

9. (Cancelled)

10. (Previously presented) The system of claim 31, further comprising a delivery catheter configured to deliver the gastric space filler to the gastric cavity via an esophagus of the patient, wherein the delivery catheter is configured to receive the gastric space filler in a collapsed state.

11. (Currently amended) A gastric space filler system, comprising: a conduit having a first end and a second end opposite the first end, wherein the first end is operably coupled to a first balloon and the second end is operably coupled to a second balloon; a first lumen through the conduit, wherein the lumen is configured for fluid infusion into the first balloon; a second lumen through the conduit, wherein the second lumen is configured for fluid infusion into the second balloon; and a third lumen extending through the conduit, wherein the third lumen is configured for instrument throughput, wherein the first and second balloons are configured to occupy a substantial volume of a gastric cavity when inflated to create a mechanical barrier that reduces food intake.

12. (Currently amended) The gastric space filler system of claim 42 wherein: the first lumen extends from the first end of the conduit to the first balloon; and the second lumen extends from the first end of the conduit to the second balloon, and wherein the first and second lumens are independently operable to control inflation and deflation of the respective balloons.

13. (Currently amended) The gastric space filler system of claim 42 wherein the third lumen extends from the first end of the conduit to a second end of the conduit, and wherein the third lumen is sized to accommodate passage of a guide wire or endoscopic instrument for therapeutic intervention.

14. (Previously presented) The gastric space filler system of claim 42, further comprising a coupling mechanism at the first end of the conduit, wherein the coupling mechanism is configured for instrument throughput into the third lumen and configured to couple to a delivery catheter and/or a filling tube.

15. (Currently amended) The gastric space filler system of claim 42 wherein the gastric space filler system is configured for delivery through an esophagus of a patient to a stomach of the patient, and wherein the system is configured to remain in the gastric cavity for a predetermined therapeutic period.

16. (Currently amended) The gastric space filler system of claim 42 wherein the conduit is configured for attachment to a delivery catheter, and wherein the third lumen of the conduit is configured to receive an instrument passed through the delivery catheter, and wherein the instrument comprises at least one of a guide wire, an endoscope, or a therapeutic delivery device.
